obligation: G099 -- one hot fragment, programs enumerated and benchmarked, Pareto frontier kept
fragment: the grouped-codec GEMV as executed at one token (K=1), which is 70.5% of the token and the hottest fragment in the program
program_space: codec x row-tiling. Enumerated by the rewrite rules the kernels already implement: a codec choice (grouped absmax at 3 or 4 bits, or 1-3 greedy binary planes) and a tiling choice (R rows sharing one activation load). Fidelity-constrained rather than strictly equivalent -- each program has a MEASURED output error, so the frontier is over (error, time).
measured_only: Every point here is measured on device. The 20 codec x R combinations that would come from assuming R's speedup multiplies across codecs are NOT included: R tiling is measured only on q4, and projecting it onto the plane kernels would be an assumption wearing a measurement's clothes. G095 made that projection; this obligation asks for a MEASURED frontier.
the_finding: SIX of nine measured programs are DOMINATED, and one of them is flat_q3 -- the codec every coherent artifact in this campaign actually uses. flat_q3 R1 sits at (err 0.1952, 0.8521 ps) and flat_q4 R8 sits at (err 0.0833, 0.7190 ps): LOWER ERROR AND LOWER TIME on both axes. Every q3 artifact is strictly worse than a q4 artifact with better tiling, on the two axes that matter. Only BPW favours q3, and G097 measured that BPW is not the currency.
the_frontier_is_three_programs: planes_k1 R1 at the cheap end (0.6059 ps, err 0.4274), planes_k2 R1 in the middle (0.6676, 0.2447), and flat_q4 R8 at the accurate end (0.7190, 0.0833). Nothing else survives. That is the receipt this obligation asks for -- a frontier, not a search log.
